reviews.review:
Final review: Really enjoyed this! The comparison to Xenogears isn't simply in the biblical themes and mechs, it also has that great, snappy pace and some good, unexpected humor from time to time
 
Each chapter is roughly an hour, and while the dungeons have a pretty consistent flow, each chapter adds something new to play around with in terms of builds. The story itself never felt formulaic ; each time it felt like it would start, there'd be a turn that kept me engaged.

The story is an interesting take on Jesus, and I think managed to be dramatic and engaging throughout. While the other games aren't required, there's some nice pay-off for anyone that's played through Elohim Eternal 1 and Exodus (the latter of which is free, and while I felt it sticks too closely to the story of Moses, does have a good ending that directly ties into the world of 2).

Excited to see where this series goes!


Original review: Will update after finishing, but really enjoying the game so far! The summaries of the first game and free story really help refresh the scenario and understand how much this second game is building on those foundations. 

So far, the battles are similar to the first, which isn't a bad thing! Attacking enemy weaknesses is heavily encouraged, and techniques are connected to equipment, allowing for a wide variety of builds. 

Really enjoying the aesthetic and the music in episode 2! Excited to see where it goes, but want to get an early review out to encourage others to give this game a chance.
